script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. TECH STARTUP - DAY

The office is buzzing with energy. People are chatting, typing on laptops, and occasionally laughing. At the front of the room, a whiteboard is filled with ideas.

JANE (30s, ambitious), a project manager, addresses her team.

JANE
(upbeat)
Alright everyone, we've got a tight deadline on this one. Let's make it happen.

As Jane speaks, the door swings open and in walks MARK (40s, stern). He's the CEO of the company.

MARK
(to Jane)
Jane, could I speak with you in private?

INT. JANE'S OFFICE - DAY

Jane sits at her desk, and Mark stands in front of her.

MARK
(serious)
Jane, I've been watching your team closely. You're doing great work, but I've noticed something that concerns me.

JANE
(defensive)
What is it?

MARK
(sighs)
You've been putting in long hours, and I know you're dedicated, but you're not giving yourself enough time to rest. You've also been snapping at people unnecessarily. I don't want to see you burn out.

JANE
(surprised)
I didn't realize it was that bad.

MARK
(nods)
I understand that this project is important, but it's not worth sacrificing your health and the morale of your team.

JANE
(quietly)
I'll make sure to take better care of myself.

MARK
(smiles)
I believe in you, Jane. Let's work together to make this project a success while also taking care of ourselves.

INT. TECH STARTUP - DAY

Later that day, Jane is in the break room, making a cup of tea. SARAH (20s, friendly), a new team member, enters.

SARAH
(excited)
Hey Jane, I heard you're the project manager for our new project. I'd love to learn from you.

JANE
(smiling)
Of course, Sarah. I'm always happy to help.

As they chat, Jane shares some tips and advice with Sarah. This interaction is a turning point for Jane, as it reminds her of the importance of mentoring and helping others.

INT. TECH STARTUP - DAY

A few days later, the team is working late into the night, and tensions are high. Suddenly, the power goes out, and the team is plunged into darkness.

JANE
(frustrated)
This is unacceptable. We have a deadline to meet!

MARK enters the room, carrying a flashlight.

MARK
(calmly)
Jane, everyone needs a break sometimes. Let's take this opportunity to recharge and come back to the project with renewed energy.

JANE
(sighs)
You're right. Let's go home and come back tomorrow.

INT. TECH STARTUP - NEXT DAY

The team returns to the office, refreshed and ready to tackle the project with renewed energy. Jane leads the team, but she makes sure to delegate tasks and take breaks herself.

INT. TECH STARTUP - DAY

The project is a success, and the team celebrates. Jane looks around the room, proud of what they've accomplished, and grateful for the opportunity to learn and grow.

MARK
(raising a glass)
To a successful project and to taking care of ourselves in the process.

JANE
(smiling)
Cheers to that.

FADE OUT.

END OF SCREENPLAY.
